name: maybe_Ui_List_MoveCursorToFreeCell

The caller 0x003BD008 uses the empty record as 'no free cell', so 'free' is still only the caller's interpretation: the accept test itself is a pure hit-test.
evidence: NEW (negative): its only caller is the still-tentative maybe_Ui_List_FindFirstFreeSlot (0x003BD008, 0.45), and the accept callee is the geometric maybe_Ui_List_CellMatchesAtPoint (0x00642248, refined at 0.49 in R3_071). Both the 'cursor' and 'free' wording therefore remain the caller's semantics; only the grid scan and the CellMatchesAtPoint test are proven.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcRandomScaleVector
signature: void maybe_Battle_CalcRandomScaleVector(float* out, float* src, float scaleBias)
summary: Writes out[0..2] = src[+0x1C,+0x20,+0x24] * (4.0 + uniform[-0.5,0.5] + scaleBias), where the random value comes from the battle RNG at battleWork+0x4218, then overwrites out[1] with the unscaled src[+0x20]. A small random-jitter scale helper; the old 'ActionAnimObject' class label is not supported by anything in the body.
evidence: NEW: disassembly read by hand - vmov s16,s0; bl 0x001CA3E4(battleRng,0) with s0=-0.5f (0xBF000000) and s1=+0.5f (0x3F000000); vadd s0 = s0 + 4.0f (0x40800000) + s16; three vmul by src[+0x1C..+0x24]; vstr out[2], vstmia out{0,1}, then str [r5,#0x20] into out+4. The batch's caller list is not trustworthy (Ui_PartyStatus_AdjustValue's region contains no reference to 0x003CE3D8), so the previous Battle_ActionAnimObject class prefix was an invention; the battle-RNG identity is the part that is real.

name: maybe_Gfx_BindMaterialSet

No caller, so the owner class (previously guessed ScriptContext) is still unproven.
evidence: NEW: every callee is now named and consistent with a one-shot material-set bind/submit/release (Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant, Gfx_MaterialSet_Release, Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault), and the packet resolve 0x005F5818 is the same handle resolver used by Battle2DUnit_Dtor. But the function has neither a caller nor a vtable slot, so the 'self' class stays unknown; kept below 0.5.

Also corrected the return type: the body returns nothing, so this is void, not UiResourceList*.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_Finish
signature: void maybe_Save_LoadTask_Finish(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

Both a finished save/load task and a UI window/child teardown fit this body.
evidence: NEW (negative): the address has no readable C in decomp/readable (only the 0-byte recovered stub), its batch caller list is the usual neighbourhood noise, and none of its four callees (0x0062F070, 0x0010EBD8, 0x006722D8, 0x002CDB5C) carries a name. Only Ui_UiManager_GetInstance and the +0x718/+0x820/+0x824 field layout are real, so the save/load reading stays a hypothesis.

name: Party_GetCharacterIdAtSlot
summary: Asks the object's vtable +0x88 accessor for the selected party slot (-1 = no selection) and returns the per-slot character id byte from the party table at (work+0x24A98)+slot+4, or 0xFF when no slot is selected. Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers uses it to learn which member is currently in the slot being swapped.
evidence: NEW: the sole caller is now the named Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers, and the callee 0x0066B0E4 is a byte getter (disassembly: add r0,r0,r1; ldrb r0,[r0,#4]) addressed from work+0x24A98 - the bag/party work block - so the value really is the slot's character id with the 0xFF empty sentinel.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObjectCtor_vt773258

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick3107_UpdateAction

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseHandle
signature: void maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseHandle(void* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)

The caller passes (work+8)->f_54, i.e. the Field_ObjectManager, so the released object is a field object owned by the panel, not a UI drawable. The Ui_Overlay class label still comes only from the tentative caller 0x001E3B40, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_MessageWindow_DtorDelete

name: maybe_Event_Gimmick_UpdateOffset
summary: State-2 update of the event-gimmick offset animation: multiplies f_38 by 0.8 per call, and either writes the remaining offset into the sampled node's +0x9C or, once it is <= 0.5, samples the node transform (0x003DD068) into f_3C..f_45 and advances the state byte f_2C to 3.

name: maybe_Event_Gimmick_CheckDone

The predicate-style 'CheckDone' flag does not apply: this is a void state-machine step that mutates f_2C, so there is no dropped return value. The class still rests on the vtable only, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Container_HashMap_LookupBySlot
signature: void* maybe_Container_HashMap_LookupBySlot(void* self, unsigned int ignored, unsigned int slot)

evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0050D6A4 is now std_String_InitFrom and 0x00658C38 is the bucket key compare used by the cache-index writer, which supports the two-table hash layout. The body still contains the lost in_ZR flag that selects the small table, so the branch condition is not trustworthy; kept below 0.5.

name: Os_InvokeCallbacksVariant
summary: Second copy of the OS pending-callback dispatcher: when (pending & ~handled) is set, invokes up to eight registered callbacks, drains the runtime event, sends the close request and clears the pending flags; unlike Os_InvokeCallbacks (0x00118814) it also writes the handled state (0/1) into block[0] before returning it.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x00118814 is now named Os_InvokeCallbacks (0.50) and the two bodies are identical except for the final handled-byte store in this copy (disassembly writes 0/1 to 0x007AEA00), so the variant relationship is proven; only the suffix 'Variant' remains purely descriptive.

name: Err_WaitForStatusFlags
summary: Wait helper of the CTR SDK nn::err (err:f) client: clears the one-byte state at 0x007AE954, runs the two state hooks 0x00113A40(3)/0x001143C8(0), then polls the status query until the returned status word shares a set bit with both of the two flag bytes it also returns (sleeping 10,000,000 ticks per poll), and restores the saved state at 0x007AE954 afterwards.
evidence: NEW: FACTS.md records 0x0051BA34..0x0051CD40 as the CTR SDK nn::err (err:f) fatal-error applet library, and this address sits inside that range; both callers are the err paths 0x0051BA38 (fatal-result check) and 0x0051CCFC (throw). The old Sound_ prefix came from the equally poisoned Sound_* labels in the same range - 0x007AE954 lies in the OS IPC state block next to the 0x007AE910 session state used by Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest, not in a sound object.

name: Script_EventVm_Init
summary: Creates the Squirrel VM used by an event script: Script_Vm_Create with an 0x40-entry stack, registers the default table members, installs the 0x0055A4D8 callback, finalises the VM, stores it at self+0x24 and clears the two-word global at 0x0083876C.

name: Gfx_SpriteParts_AppendRecord

summary: Appends one 40-byte (0x28) part record to the sprite-part builder's second vector: a 16-byte generated key (0x00665618), two u64 values from the source record and the u16 index, growing the vector through std_Vector40_Reserve and advancing the write cursor by 0x28.
evidence: NEW: caller Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart40 (named) builds its parts with exactly this call, and the reserve helper is the now-named std_Vector40_Reserve whose 40-byte element matches the ten words (0x28 bytes) written here; the earlier 'Add40' wording was already replaced by 'AppendRecord', which the body confirms.

name: Battle_Ui_UpdateScrollAnimation
signature: bool Battle_Ui_UpdateScrollAnimation(void* anim, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

Driven by g_battleUiScrollAnimTable and a 0x2388-frame base.
evidence: NEW: the sole caller is now the named Battle_Ui_UpdateItemCommand, which calls it while the item-command window is moving, and the callee is maybe_Battle_Ui_ApplyScrollOffset; the per-slot interpolation and the 8-slot table are visible, so the animation stepper is confirmed even though the individual state labels are not.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor(u8* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

evidence: NEW: the caller 0x001F1BEC is still only maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor, and the element type 0x00192580 is shared with the party-stat code (0x001924DC Party_Member_RecalcStatsFromCommand), so the block's role is plausible but neither the owning screen nor the element semantics is confirmed; kept below 0.5.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbA
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkDirectionThumbA(char* grid, u32* outCollision, u32 x, u32 y)
summary: Four-byte Thumb entry that falls through into the shared 0x005BEF5A collision-step walker with direction register 0 (its B twin differs only in that register): walks the actor's candidate chips, calls Field2D_MapChip_CheckCollisionStep for each hit and copies the 0xD-byte step records before finishing through the actor's vtable +0x40.
evidence: NEW (negative): there is no caller and the recovered C is dominated by Ghidra damage (unaff_r6/r7/r10, in_stack_* pseudolocals, in_OV), so only the two named callees Field2D_MapChip_CheckCollisionStep and std_memcpy are trustworthy; the 'A' direction is an interpretation of the four bytes of entry code, not of the C.

signature: void Field2D_MapChip_SelectEntry(u16* out, void* src, int useAlternate)
summary: Selects one entry of the 2D map-chip style table: when the global override byte 0x007A6AE6 is not -1 it returns that fixed index, otherwise it scans the table for the first entry whose id differs from 0xFFFF and whose flag byte passes the 0x005BCA50 test, returning {u16 id, u16 index} (or 0xFFFF / -1).
evidence: NEW: the caller list is now twelve functions all belonging to the Field2D_MapChip / Field2D_Sprite family (BuildCollisionMask, CheckCollisionStep, QuerySightLine, CalcChipDistance, DispatchDraw, UpdateLighting, RenderObjectBatch, CalcChipDistance...), which fixes the table's subsystem; what the entry semantically is (style/terrain/attribute) is still unnamed, hence the deliberately generic verb 'SelectEntry'.

name: maybe_Field2D_SpriteNode_InitFromParams
signature: int maybe_Field2D_SpriteNode_InitFromParams(u32* self, int* arg2, int arg3, u32* params)
summary: Initialises a 2D sprite node from a parameter block: installs vtable 0x00783870, copies three parameter words, derives the position through Gfx_Actor_SetPositionXY, stores a 40.0f vertical scale and attaches the sprite handle through 0x0017C4CC / 0x0029E488. Called from Field2D_Sprite_SetRotation before the sprite is used.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the named Field2D_Sprite_SetRotation and the position helper Gfx_Actor_SetPositionXY is named, which supports the sprite-node setup; the parameter-block layout is only partly readable and vtable 0x00783870 has no symbol, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_Trail_ClampProgress
summary: Trail update step: fetches the curve/sample array through the object's vtable +0x70, clamps the two progress floats, writes the clamped progress and rebinds the trail animator (Anim_Resource_Bind). The body is heavily damaged, so only the caller and the animator rebind are trustworthy.

name: Ui_Overlay_IsRectLargerThanScreen
summary: In game mode, for an active overlay host (f_8E set, f_74 present, flag +0x12 clear) returns 1 when its rectangle (f_98..f_A4) is wider than 320.0 or taller than 240.0 - the 3DS screen size - and 0 otherwise. It tests only the size, never the position.

The old summary's '~314' was a misread of the integer form.

name: Party_CountExtraSkillSlots
summary: Counts how many of the two u16 ids at member+0x19A / +0x19C pass the same learned-skill predicate (0x006C29A0) that Party_CountLearnedSkills uses for the 60-entry list at +0x122. The party stat calculation (Party_StatCalc_ApplyBaseStats / SetupMemberContext) consumes the count.
evidence: NEW: the twin 0x006291A8 is now named Party_CountLearnedSkills (0.60) and uses the identical predicate over +0x122..+0x19A, which fixes both the predicate and the record; this function is the same count over the two slots immediately before the +0x19E active-state array. What the two slots mean semantically is still unknown, but 'extra skill slots' is a faithful description of the operation.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitReelStrip
summary: Constructs a 27-element array of 4-byte elements (element constructor 0x005F9720) in the caller's stack frame. The only caller is Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult, which consumes it as one reel strip; the initialiser itself touches no symbol table.
evidence: NEW: the caller is now the named Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult (0.55), which uses 24-stop / 5-column reel data, so the casino context is fixed; the function only performs std_ConstructArray(..., 0x005F9720, 4, 0x1B), and no reel constant or symbol is read here, so 'reel strip' remains the caller's interpretation.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitPaytable
summary: Zeroes a five-byte header with two 0xFF sentinels and constructs three 4-byte elements (constructor 0x005F9720) in the caller's stack frame; the payout arithmetic is not in this function.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult (0.55) but the body reads no paytable constant and the three-element array is never dereferenced here, so 'paytable' is still only a guess from the neighbour; kept below 0.5. The 912-byte size in the header does not match the few visible lines, so the readable body is probably truncated as well.

name: Casino_Slot_PickStopBySymbol
signature: u32 Casino_Slot_PickStopBySymbol(int* reelData, int reel, u32 symbol, int shiftMode, int matchEqual)
summary: Collects the 24 stops of reel column 'reel' whose symbol equals 'symbol' (or differs from it when matchEqual is 0, skipping symbol 6), shuffles that candidate list with the slot-machine shuffle state and returns the chosen stop index, optionally rotated by one/two stops for shiftMode 1/2.
evidence: NEW: Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult (0.55) calls it five times with reel 0..4 and symbol 5 in the forced-jackpot path, and the body's column table g_slotReelColumnOffset plus the 5-stride 24-entry reel layout match that caller exactly. The eight unrelated 'callers' in the batch come from the noisy merged call graph - the asm region files for Ui_PartyStatus-style callers contain no reference to this address - so they no longer block promotion.

name: maybe_Data_ResolveRelativeEntry8OrTrap
signature: void* maybe_Data_ResolveRelativeEntry8OrTrap(u16* key, void* group, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Resolves an entry through a relative-offset link chain: follows key[2] (an offset relative to key+4), and when the chain is broken re-resolves the id through Game_GetDataManager + 0x0063CDD8 using key[0] minus the group's base id; every failure path calls 0x00707BD4 (the string-format assert) and returns the static default entry 0x0066C0A0+4.
evidence: NEW: the data-manager path is now the named Game_GetDataManager and the record lookup 0x0063CDD8 is the ItemRecord accessor documented in FACTS.md, which pins the fallback to an item-table entry; the assert helper 0x00707BD4 is still unnamed and the caller set is only Gfx_EffectObject_Replace / Ui_Window_RefreshEffect / maybe_Ui_Pane_CreateEffectForItemId, so the generic 'resolve relative entry or trap' wording is kept.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_WriteMaterialColor
summary: Emits the material/colour GPU state: converts the current material's float colour and the light-scale values to the PICA 21-bit float format and appends them, together with the material, texture-env and light register writes (0x000F0040/41/43...), as (value, command) pairs to the command buffer at 0x007AED34.
evidence: NEW: the only caller is now the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0.60) and it dispatches here for the material/colour dirty bit, so the role as one per-dirty-bit state writer is confirmed; the individual PICA register numbers are still read from the 0x000F00xx command words rather than from a register-name table, so the precise 'material colour' label keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_SyncTextureStage
summary: Synchronises the cached texture-stage state: compares the render node's two resource pointers with the cached ones, returns when nothing changed, otherwise emits the 0x000F011x / 0x000F006E register pairs and rebuilds the sampler state.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0.60), confirming this is a dirty-bit-0x100 state writer, but the body still keeps one pointer in in_r3/unaff_r7 and the FP status in in_fpscr, so the cache comparison is only partly reconstructed and the confidence stays at 0.40.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuState_BuildLightingBlock
signature: void maybe_Gfx_GpuState_BuildLightingBlock(void* self, u32 dirtyBits, u32 mode, u32* out)
summary: Large GPU-state rebuild routine: for the given dirty bits it emits the 0x000F00xx register writes for the viewport/scissor/window block, the texture-binding block, the light/lighting block and the shader-constant block into the command buffer at 0x007AED34.
evidence: NEW (negative): the only caller is the named Gfx_GpuState_Invalidate (0.60), which confirms it is one of the per-dirty-bit state writers, but the 3454-byte body is heavily damaged (unaff_r6/r7/r9, in_cr0/1/2/4/5/9, coprocessor_* and halt_baddata), so only the 'writes several register blocks' part is real and even 'lighting' is inferred from the 0x000F00xx range.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRow
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_WrapRow(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int wrap)
summary: Adds delta to the list's current row index (+0x4C) and, when the result goes negative and wrap is set, wraps it back into range using the item count from vtable +0x64. The upper clamp and the delta==0 case are lost to three bad-instruction truncations.
evidence: NEW (negative): the callers (Ui_SakusenWindow_Confirm, Ui_ScrollBar_Update) only show it moves the list cursor; the body ends in three halt_baddata() sites and an indirect call through address 0, so the lost upper clamp means even 'WrapRow' is only half proven - kept at 0.30.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_ScrollByAnimated
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_ScrollByAnimated(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int scroll)
summary: Animated scroll of a list pane: adds delta to the row/scroll index, clamps it against the item count, either recentres the pane on the cursor (scroll == 0) or clamps a negative index and selects the new entry, then refreshes through the window's virtual +0x60.
evidence: NEW (negative): the only caller is the named Ui_EquipWindow_PushSelectPane, so it is a list-pane scroll; but the body has bad instruction data plus an indirect call through address 0, and unaff_r6/unaff_r7, so only the clamp/recentre shape is trustworthy.

name: maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple
signature: void maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenSimple(void* self, u8 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Minimal data-panel open: rewinds the embedded pane buffer (+0xE3C4 = 0), copies the three pane words from game work +0x2FB18..+0x2FB20, rebinds the pane through 0x0051BB08 with id 0xC, sets the pane state to 9 and locks +0xE118.
evidence: NEW (negative): there is still no caller and none of the three helpers (0x0010F300, 0x0051BB08, mutex lock) carries a name that would identify the panel; only the state word 9 and the +0x2FB18 pane source are certain, so both 'DataPanel' and 'OpenSimple' remain guesses.

name: maybe_Snd_BeginFrame
summary: Frame prologue for one of the IPC-backed stream contexts: when the queue flags allow it, sets the completion event, publishes the current buffer pointer from 0x7EF3C4 + 0xC0, clears the two dirty flags, executes a data-synchronisation barrier and takes the mutex at +8.
evidence: NEW (negative): the body contains a broken expression (`*0x007AEA98 0x007AEA98[1]`) and its four callees are from unrelated subsystems (Input_SetPadMode, Gfx_UpdateTextureBindings, Svc_Cecd_Cmd000AB, Os_UnlockMonitor), so the previous module correction (Snd_ rather than Gfx_) is itself only a label match on the 0x10C8C4/0x112E38/0x1132DC helper cluster; kept below 0.5.

name: maybe_Actor_ApplyStateFlags
signature: void maybe_Actor_ApplyStateFlags(void* self, u32* flags, u32 arg3)
summary: Applies a request/state flag block to an actor: handles the facing bit (sets f_7C to arg3, 4 or 1 depending on flags->f_14), copies the shadow/offset pair from 0x007C9980 when bit 0x40 is set, clears the handled bits from self->f_6C and re-queues the remaining mask in flags+4 before signalling the global mutex.
evidence: NEW: the only named callee is Os_MutexLock(&g_globalMutexObject), which confirms the 'publish/queue remaining flags' tail, and the field writes (f_7C facing, f_70/f_74 offset/shadow, f_6C pending mask) match the actor-update layout used by the field actor code; but the only caller set is empty and no vtable names this method, so it keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Os_SetRuntimeFlag
summary: Small one-shot hook: takes the runtime lock object at 0x007AE4A0 through 0x00111D50 and sets the byte at 0x007AE49D to 1. The flag owner is not visible, so the exact runtime state it announces is unknown.
evidence: NEW: disassembly confirms the lock object is loaded from the literal 0x007AE4A0 immediately before the call (ldr r0,[pc,#0x14] at 0x0010643C) and the store is the byte at 0x007AE49D, so 'lock + set runtime flag' is exactly right; the meaning of the flag is still unknown and the function has no caller, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Script_SqValueList_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the Squirrel value-list holder: installs vtable 0x007589F4, clears the two link/refcount words and default-constructs the single 8-byte SQObjectPtr at +0x2C. Byte-identical twin of 0x0018BE68, i.e. the two template copies emitted for two different owners.
evidence: NEW: the destructor 0x0018BF48 (maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor) and the accessor 0x0018BBB0 (Script_SqValueList_GetItem, 0.50) both use the same vtable 0x007589F4 and the same 8-byte SQObjectPtr element at +0x2C, which fixes the class; the ctor shape (vtable + one inline element) is unambiguous, so the name is promoted while the A/B twin suffix is kept because the two addresses are separate template copies.

name: Script_SqValueList_CtorB
summary: Second, byte-identical constructor of the Squirrel value-list holder (same vtable 0x007589F4, same single 8-byte SQObjectPtr at +0x2C): the 'B' copy emitted for the other owner.
evidence: NEW: same vtable and same element as the now-named destructor/accessor pair (0x0018BF48, 0x0018BBB0), and the body is byte-identical to 0x0018BD88 - the only open question is which owner this template copy belongs to, which is why it keeps the B suffix rather than a class name.

name: Message_FormatArgSlotPool_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the formatted-message argument-slot pool: installs vtable 0x0075B3BC and default-constructs the sixteen 0x108-byte argument slots immediately after the vtable word. Ui_Core_Init allocates the 0x1084-byte block, and the pool is the object behind the *0x007AC834 slot singleton that Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset clears.
evidence: NEW: the matching destructor 0x001F0B80 installs the same vtable 0x0075B3BC, clears the global *0x007AC834 and destroys exactly sixteen 0x108-byte entries - the array this ctor builds; the parallel R3_033 refine batch re-identified that destructor as Message_FormatArgSlotPool_DtorDelete (0.60), and FACTS.md fixes *0x007AC834 as the 0x108-stride formatted-message argument-slot singleton. That renames the old generic 'Ui_System_CreateSlotArray' to the real class.

name: maybe_Text_Window_RestoreEntryState
summary: Resets a message-window entry to its 'no message' state (ids 0 / 0xFFFF / 0) when the current entry object is missing, then, if f_230 is a valid index into the record table at f_10 (count +0x60, relative array +0x58->+0x24, stride 0x20), rebuilds the 0x80-entry local record buffer and copies the shared 2-float pivot from 0x0072A944 into self+0x30/+0x34.
evidence: NEW (negative): there is still no caller and no named callee that identifies the record table (0x004777D4 is unnamed), so the container layout remains only a match against the same 0x60/0x58->0x24 pattern used elsewhere; the body also ends in a 'Subroutine does not return' ConstructArray, so the readable C is probably truncated. Kept below 0.5.
